paragraphs.text: Halifax II BB320 belonged to 1656 Heavy Conversion Unit and took off from RAF Lindholme on a training night navigation exercise. It emerged from cloud spinning and crashed near Cheadle, Staffordshire, on 7 February 1944. All six crew died.

The crew were Flying Officer Ernest Richards (pilot, 26), Flying Officer Hubert Kerr of the RCAF (air bomber, 28), Sergeant Kenneth Murray (navigator, 23), Sergeant Albert Denny (flight engineer, 28), Sergeant William Joshua (wireless operator/air gunner, 22) and Sergeant Herbert Couling (air gunner, 20).
They were buried at Chester (Blacon) Cemetery (Richards, Kerr and Couling), Darlington West Cemetery (Murray), Sarn Cemetery (Joshua) and Streatham Cemetery (Denny).

A brass plaque on the wall of Blakeley Lane Methodist Chapel names the crew. It was unveiled on 7 February 2020. The Leek Post & Times reported that Kingsley Parish Council funded it, and that the story was rediscovered by local historian Martyn Hordern.

photos.credit: Martyn Horden, via IWM War Memorials Register
photos.caption: The BB320 brass plaque on Blakeley Lane Methodist Chapel.

notes: Crew all identified (6 of 6) from IBCC, with CWGC for Denny only; IBCC pages for the other five were each a single institutional source (CWGC pages for them not opened). Our current record gives Kerr as Pilot and Richards as 'Crew'; IBCC has Richards as pilot and Kerr as air bomber. Location conflict: IWM says near Werrington; Leek Post and IBCC point to Kingsley Moor / near Cheadle (location_name conflict recorded, not resolved). Timing: IBCC says 'night navigation exercise' but also lists the raid as 'Day'; Leek Post (via search extract only, page 403) says about 6.30pm. The Leek Post extract also said all crew were dead apart from the rear gunner, who was mortally wounded; this was not confirmed at source and no IBCC record gives a different date of death, so it is not claimed. The Leek Post 'Kingsley Parish Council funded the plaque' claim rests on that one unverified-secondary source. Custodian: the chapel hosts the plaque and our record names the church as custodian, but no source read states who maintains it; kept unknown. IBCC also records a stencilled wooden board at St Edward the Confessor Church, Leek, and a group tablet at Bawtry Hall; neither is claimed here. No squadron-association, Peak District air crash or ASN page for BB320 was found. Chapel spelled Blakeley (IWM, Leek Post) and Blakely (IBCC). Squadron: 1656 HCU is a conversion unit, not a squadron.
